legend: There is an invasive ductal component in addition to the mucinous component (the mixed type of mucinous carcinoma).

An in situ component in mucinous carcinoma of the skin is a strong indicator of primary cutaneous origin; in situ lesions range from various types of ductal hyperplasia to ductal carcinoma in situ. The in situ component corresponds to ductal carcinoma in situ of micropapillary type.

Neoplastic cells are arranged in nests, strands, or individual units floating in lakes of extracellular mucin, separated by variably thick fibrous septa. In this lesion, extracellular mucin constitutes > 90% (the pure type of mucinous carcinoma).

An in situ component in mucinous carcinoma of the skin is a strong indicator of primary cutaneous origin; in situ lesions range from various types of ductal hyperplasia to ductal carcinoma in situ. Staining for calponin highlights preserved basal/myoepithelial cells in the ductal carcinoma in situ.

Small basaloid nests with ducts and intracytoplasmic lumina dispersed in lakes of mucinous stroma that extend into the subcutis. Mucin is compartmentalized by delicate fibrous stoma, creating a honeycomb appearance. Little pleomorphism and few mitosis are seen.
